en: The Questions of Milinda, Chapter on Duration, 4. The Question on the Person Who Experiences Reconnection "Venerable sir, is there a person who experiences reconnection? "There is, great king. "But, venerable sir, what kind of person reconnects? "Great king, it is the person who possesses wholesome roots that reconnects. "But, venerable sir, does the wholesome root reconnect? "No, great king. "If the wholesome root does not reconnect, venerable sir, then how does the person reconnect? "Great king, it is by means of the wholesome root that the person reconnects. "Just as, great king, a man might have a lamp brought from one village to another; would the flame of the lamp go from that first village to the second? "No, venerable sir. "But, great king, without the flame of the lamp, would that man be able to bring the lamp from the first village to the second? "No, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, it is by means of the wholesome root that the person reconnects. "Venerable sir, is there a person who experiences final Nibbāna? "There is, great king. "But, venerable sir, what kind of person attains final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is the person who possesses wholesome roots that attains final Nibbāna. "But, venerable sir, do the wholesome roots attain final Nibbāna? "No, great king. "If the wholesome roots do not attain final Nibbāna, venerable sir, then how does the person attain final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is by means of the wholesome roots that the person attains final Nibbāna. "Just as, great king, a man might have a lamp brought from one village to another until he reaches his own home; would the flame of the lamp go all the way from the first village to his own home? "Yes, venerable sir. "But, great king, without the flame of the lamp, would that man be able to reach his own home? "No, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, it is by means of the wholesome roots that the person attains final Nibbāna. "Venerable sir, is there a person who experiences both reconnection and final Nibbāna? "There is, great king. "But, venerable sir, what kind of person experiences both reconnection and final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is the person who possesses wholesome roots that experiences both reconnection and final Nibbāna. "But, venerable sir, do the wholesome roots experience both reconnection and final Nibbāna? "No, great king. "If the wholesome roots do not experience both reconnection and final Nibbāna, venerable sir, then how does the person experience both reconnection and final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is by means of the wholesome roots that the person experiences both reconnection and final Nibbāna. "Just as, great king, a man might have a lamp brought from one village to another until he reaches his own home; would the flame of the lamp go all the way from the first village to his own home? "Yes, venerable sir. "But, great king, without the flame of the lamp, would that man be able to reach his own home? "No, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, it is by means of the wholesome roots that the person experiences both reconnection and final Nibbāna. "Venerable sir, is there a person who experiences neither reconnection nor final Nibbāna? "There is, great king. "But, venerable sir, what kind of person experiences neither reconnection nor final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is the person who possesses unwholesome roots and has abandoned the wholesome roots that experiences neither reconnection nor final Nibbāna. "But, venerable sir, do the unwholesome roots experience neither reconnection nor final Nibbāna? "No, great king. "If the unwholesome roots do not experience neither reconnection nor final Nibbāna, venerable sir, then how does the person experience neither reconnection nor final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is by means of the unwholesome roots that the person experiences neither reconnection nor final Nibbāna. "Just as, great king, a man might have a lamp brought from one village to another until he reaches his own home; would the flame of the lamp go all the way from the first village to his own home? "No, venerable sir. "But, great king, without the flame of the lamp, would that man be able to reach his own home? "No, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, it is by means of the unwholesome roots that the person experiences neither reconnection nor final Nibbāna. "Venerable sir, is there a person who experiences reconnection and does not experience final Nibbāna? "There is, great king. "But, venerable sir, what kind of person reconnects and does not attain final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is the person who possesses wholesome roots but has not yet abandoned the unwholesome roots that reconnects and does not attain final Nibbāna.

"But, venerable sir, do the wholesome roots reconnect and not attain final Nibbāna? "No, great king. "If the wholesome roots do not reconnect and not attain final Nibbāna, venerable sir, then how does the person reconnect and not attain final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is by means of the wholesome roots that the person reconnects and does not attain final Nibbāna. "Just as, great king, a man might have a lamp brought from one village to another until he reaches his own home; would the flame of the lamp go all the way from the first village to his own home? "No, venerable sir. "But, great king, without the flame of the lamp, would that man be able to reach his own home? "No, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, it is by means of the wholesome roots that the person reconnects and does not attain final Nibbāna. "Venerable sir, is there a person who attains final Nibbāna and does not reconnect? "There is, great king. "But, venerable sir, what kind of person attains final Nibbāna and does not reconnect? "Great king, it is the person who possesses wholesome roots and has abandoned the unwholesome roots that attains final Nibbāna and does not reconnect. "But, venerable sir, do the wholesome roots attain final Nibbāna and not reconnect? "No, great king. "If the wholesome roots do not attain final Nibbāna and not reconnect, venerable sir, then how does the person attain final Nibbāna and not reconnect? "Great king, it is by means of the wholesome roots that the person attains final Nibbāna and does not reconnect. "Just as, great king, a man might have a lamp brought from one village to another until he reaches his own home; would the flame of the lamp go all the way from the first village to his own home? "Yes, venerable sir. "But, great king, without the flame of the lamp, would that man be able to reach his own home? "No, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, it is by means of the wholesome roots that the person attains final Nibbāna and does not reconnect. "Venerable sir, is there a person who neither reconnects nor attains final Nibbāna? "There is, great king. "But, venerable sir, what kind of person neither reconnects nor attains final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is the person who possesses unwholesome roots and has abandoned the wholesome roots that neither reconnects nor attains final Nibbāna. "But, venerable sir, do the unwholesome roots neither reconnect nor attain final Nibbāna? "No, great king. "If the unwholesome roots do not neither reconnect nor attain final Nibbāna, venerable sir, then how does the person neither reconnect nor attain final Nibbāna? "Great king, it is by means of the unwholesome roots that the person neither reconnects nor attains final Nibbāna. "Just as, great king, a man might have a lamp brought from one village to another until he reaches his own home; would the flame of the lamp go all the way from the first village to his own home? "No, venerable sir. "But, great king, without the flame of the lamp, would that man be able to reach his own home? "No, venerable sir. "In the same way, great king, it is by means of the unwholesome roots that the person neither reconnects nor attains final Nibbāna. "Venerable sir, is there a person who reconnects and also attains
The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, does one who is not reborn experience any feeling of suffering?
The Elder replied:
“He feels something, he does not feel something.
“What does he feel, and what does he not feel?
“He feels bodily feeling, Great King, but he does not feel mental feeling.”
“Venerable sir, how does one experience bodily feeling, and how does one not experience mental feeling?

“Because the cause and the condition for the arising of bodily painful feeling have not ceased, one experiences bodily painful feeling; because the cause and the condition for mental painful feeling...”
“Because of the cessation of that cause, that condition for its arising, he does not experience mental painful feeling.
This was also said, Great King, by the Blessed One:
‘He experiences one kind of feeling: bodily, not mental.’”
“Venerable Nāgasena, why does one who experiences a painful feeling not attain final nibbāna?
“There is, Great King, neither attraction nor repulsion in an Arahant. Furthermore, Great King, Arahants do not force what is unripe; the wise wait for it to reach full maturity.
This was said, Great King, by the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma:”
“I do not rejoice in death,
nor do I rejoice in life;
I await my time.”
Like a wage-earner seeking his wages,
I do not delight in death,
nor do I delight in life.
"And I await my time,
fully aware and mindful. "You are skillful,
venerable Nāgasena," [he said].
The fourth question: On the person who reconnects and the one who experiences [the result].
